tasks.title: Create scripts/task-router.ts — task target routing module
tasks.context:
Create a new TypeScript module at scripts/task-router.ts that handles task routing based on a task_target field in sprint JSON tasks.

The module must export:

1. type TaskTarget = 'local' | 'cloud-code' | 'cloud-exec' | 'cloud-post'

2. TIMEOUT_BUDGETS: Record<TaskTarget, number> = { local: 600000, 'cloud-code': 120000, 'cloud-exec': 90000, 'cloud-post': 30000 }

3. interface TaskRoute { provider: 'ollama'|'minimax'|'anthropic'|'external'; model: string; endpoint: string; timeoutMs: number; target: TaskTarget }

4. interface RoutingLogEntry { execution_id: string; sprint_id: string; task_id: string; task_target: TaskTarget; provider: string; model: string; queued_at: string; executed_at?: string; execution_source: string; vault_reachable?: boolean; queued_local?: boolean; error?: string }

5. resolveRoute(target: TaskTarget): TaskRoute — maps target to provider/model/endpoint/timeout:
   - local: provider='ollama', model=process.env.VAULT_MODEL??'qwen3:14b', endpoint=process.env.VAULT_OLLAMA_URL??'http://vault:11434'
   - cloud-code: provider='minimax', model='MiniMax-M2.5', endpoint='https://api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions'
   - cloud-exec: provider='anthropic', model='claude-sonnet-4-20250514', endpoint='https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages'
   - cloud-post: provider='external', model='n/a', endpoint=''
   - default (unknown): log warning, return resolveRoute('cloud-code')

6. generateExecutionId(sprintId: string, taskId: string): string — deterministic sha256 hash of `${sprintId}:${taskId}`, hex slice 0..16. Import { createHash } from 'crypto'.

7. isAlreadyExecuted(executionId: string): boolean — reads logs/routing/executed.jsonl (if exists), returns true if any line has matching execution_id with a non-null executed_at.

8. logRoutingDecision(entry: RoutingLogEntry): void — mkdirSync logs/routing recursive, appendFileSync to logs/routing/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl (today's date). Also appendFileSync to logs/routing/executed.jsonl if entry.executed_at is set. Non-fatal: wrap in try/catch.

9. isVaultReachable(): Promise<boolean> — fetch GET ${VAULT_OLLAMA_URL}/api/tags with 3000ms AbortController timeout. Return true if resp.ok, false on any error.

10. queueLocalTask(task: Record<string,unknown>, entry: RoutingLogEntry): void — mkdirSync workspace/sprints/pending-local, writeFileSync pending-local/${entry.execution_id}.json with JSON {task, routing:{...entry, queued_local:true}}. Log the queue action.

11. dequeueLocalTask(executionId: string): void — unlinkSync workspace/sprints/pending-local/${executionId}.json if exists.

12. drainLocalQueue(): Promise<string[]> — if pending-local dir doesn't exist return []. Call isVaultReachable(), if false log and return []. Otherwise read all *.json files in pending-local, log count, return file paths array.

13. sprintRoutingSummary(sprintId: string): Record<string,number> — reads today's JSONL log, counts entries by task_target for the given sprintId.

All paths relative to process.cwd(). Use resolve/join from 'path'. Use fs functions from 'fs'.

tasks.title: Extend AgentTask interface + assessTaskComplexity for task_target in orchestrate-agents-v2.ts
Create runtime/router_server.py — FastAPI HTTP wrapper for KognaiRouter
tasks.context:
Create runtime/router_server.py — a FastAPI HTTP server that wraps KognaiRouter from router.py.

Requirements:
- Port: 11435 (configurable via ROUTER_PORT env var)
- Import KognaiRouter, Tier from router (same directory — add sys.path insert)
- CORS enabled for localhost (allow_origins wildcard localhost patterns)
- Single KognaiRouter singleton instance (shared, thread-safe for reads)

Pydantic models:
  class RouteRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str
    context_tokens: Optional[int] = 0
    force_local: Optional[bool] = None
    max_cost_usd: Optional[float] = None
    sprint_id: Optional[str] = None
    task_id: Optional[str] = None

  class RouteResponse(BaseModel):
    task_type: str
    tier: str
    model_name: str
    endpoint: str
    think_mode: bool
    reasoning: str
    estimated_cost_usd: float
    fallback_tier: Optional[str]
    timeout_budget_s: int

Tier timeout budgets dict: NANO=30, LOCAL=120, POWER=600, CLOUD=90, APEX=120

Endpoints:
  POST /route → RouteResponse
    - If req.force_local or req.max_cost_usd given: create per-request KognaiRouter with those overrides
    - Otherwise use singleton _router
    - Call r.route(req.prompt, context_tokens=req.context_tokens or 0)
    - Map decision fields to RouteResponse
    - timeout_budget_s = TIER_TIMEOUTS.get(tier_name, 90)
    - Raise HTTPException 500 on any exception

  GET /health → dict
    - Returns: status='ok', timestamp=UTC ISO string, total_tasks_routed, local_pct, avg_cost_per_task_usd, port

  GET /stats → dict
    - Returns router.stats() with tier_counts keys converted from Tier enum to .name strings

Entry point (if __name__ == '__main__'):
  port = int(os.environ.get('ROUTER_PORT', '11435'))
  uvicorn.run('router_server:app', host='0.0.0.0', port=port, log_level='info', reload=False)

Imports needed: fastapi, fastapi.middleware.cors, pydantic, uvicorn, datetime, os, sys, typing
Dependency note in docstring: pip3 install fastapi uvicorn httpx

tasks.title: Create scripts/drain-local-queue.ts — pending-local queue drain script
tasks.context:
Create scripts/drain-local-queue.ts — a short script run by PM2 cron every 5 minutes to drain the pending-local task queue when the vault becomes reachable.

The script should:
1. Import { drainLocalQueue, dequeueLocalTask, logRoutingDecision } from './task-router.js'
2. Call drainLocalQueue() which returns array of file paths (or empty if vault unreachable)
3. For each file path: read JSON file, log 'Draining: <execution_id>', dequeueLocalTask(execution_id), logRoutingDecision with executed_at = new Date().toISOString() and execution_source = 'pending-local-drain'
4. Log final count 'Drained N local task(s)'
5. Use top-level await (this is an ES module via ts-node)

Keep it under 50 lines. Import readFileSync from 'fs'. Export nothing.

issues.description: No error handling around file reads or queue operations; consider adding try/catch to handle I/O or RPC failures gracefully.

strengths: Top-level await is used appropriately in this ES module
Correct logging and routing decision format
